_comment: SHARED FIXTURE (self-description) — two independent implementations must agree on this document.
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/api.rs            (what the standalone recovery tool parses)
Web   : nmts/web/test/recovery-map.test.ts  (what the browser writes)
Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
WHAT THIS ADDS (owner directive, 2026-08-19): a document that describes ITSELF, and per-file dates.
A recovery list described the ACCOUNT thoroughly and itself barely at all. The person it is for
is holding one file years later with no site to visit: which program reads this, where is it,
where is the format written down, and WHICH CHAIN do these blob ids belong to were unanswered.
The last of those is not cosmetic — a blob id from testnet and one from mainnet are the same
kind of string, and the recovery program carried that as a documented limitation.
⛔ THE VERSION DID NOT MOVE, and must not. Every field here is additive and its ABSENCE changes
no meaning, so nmts-recovery 0.1.0 and 0.2.x read this document exactly as they read one without
it. `v` is still what the CONTENT needs — 2 for this one. A bump would have made those builds
REFUSE the file, which is the opposite of the favour it looks like — until a 1.0.0 exists a
format may run ahead of the tools, but never so that a published build refuses a file it
could read.
⚠ EVERY FIELD IS A CLAIM AND EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL. A reader must never require one, and must
never act on `created_at`/`updated_at` beyond stamping them on the files it writes: they come
from the storage layer and nothing checks them. `seq` orders the chain, as it always has.
The second item carries NO dates — what a file uploaded before the fields existed looks like.
